findings.issue_text: [BUG] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts the result of infra log.FromContext to *log.ConcreteLogger and silently falls back to d.New(), discarding the contextual attributes when the assertion fails. If infra log.FromContext returns any non-ConcreteLogger implementation, every 'Plugin Request Completed' log line emitted by LoggerMiddleware loses the pluginId/dsName/uname attributes the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware was built to inject — the feature silently becomes a no-op with no error, and log-based dashboards/alerts keyed on those fields go empty.

[BUG] The rewrite of logRequest drops the traceID log field entirely — tracing.TraceIDFromContext is removed and ContextualLoggerMiddleware never adds a traceID attribute. Operators correlating plugin request logs with traces lose the traceID join key; existing log queries/dashboards that filter 'Plugin Request Completed' events by traceID return nothing after this diff.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger(), discarding all call/log capture state on the receiver. Any existing test that shares a single TestLogger for assertions will see zero recorded calls once production code paths switch to FromContext (as LoggerMiddleware now does), producing false-passing or confusingly-empty assertions; future maintainers get bitten when migrating tests to the contextual API.

[ADVISORY] The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware is wired in the middleware chain with an implicit ordering constraint — it must sit outside LoggerMiddleware so instrumentContext's attributes are visible to LoggerMiddleware.logRequest — that is enforced only by list position, with no comment or ordering guard. The next refactor that reorders the middlewares slice (e.g. moving logger middleware for a config flag) silently breaks attribute propagation with no compile or test failure, since FromContext just falls back to an attribute-less logger.

[BUG] The 'Plugin Request Completed' egress log line silently loses the traceID field because the old explicit `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` lookup was deleted and nothing in the new FromContext path guarantees it is re-added. Operators and dashboards/alerts keyed on the grafana-data-egress log lines (e.g. joining a plugin egress event to a trace via traceID) get log entries with no traceID; the correlation requirement the previous code satisfied is dropped. It only survives if infra's ConcreteLogger.FromContext happens to re-derive it, which the diff never verifies.

[BUG] The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (69 lines of behavior-bearing logic including conditional attribute enrichment for DataSourceInstanceSettings and User) ships with zero test coverage — no test file in the diff exercises it. A regression in instrumentContext (wrong attribute keys, nil deref on DataSourceInstanceSettings fields, attributes not actually propagated to the logger) would strip pluginId/dsUID/uname from all egress logs with no failing test; the diff scanned contains only the renamed metrics_middleware_test.go, which does not touch this middleware.

[BUG] LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now depends entirely on a contextual logger having been injected by the separately-registered ContextualLoggerMiddleware, but LoggerMiddleware itself carries no guarantee of that pairing — any composition site that stacks LoggerMiddleware without the new middleware loses pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName and dsUID from every egress log. Only CreateMiddlewares was updated to add the pairing; any other construction path (tests, alternative service wiring) that composes LoggerMiddleware directly produces log lines missing all identifying fields, a silent observability regression rather than an error.

[ADVISORY] The stream endpoints SubscribeStream, PublishStream, and RunStream pass through without calling instrumentContext, so contextual attributes are absent on streaming paths even though the middleware exists specifically to add them. RunStream handlers and downstream loggers emit log lines without pluginId/dsName/uname on streaming requests; if the goal of the refactor was complete contextual logging, streams are a dropped requirement. Rebuttal: the old instrumentation middleware also skipped streams — but this middleware was created in this diff to own that job, so the gap is new surface, not preserved behavior.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts the infra logger to *log.ConcreteLogger and, on failure, silently falls back to d.New(), discarding all contextual attributes the middleware chain just attached. If infra's FromContext returns any non-Concrete implementation (e.g. a wrapped or fallback logger in tests or future refactors), the 'Plugin Request Completed' line loses pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname with no error or signal — the same observability regression the refactor was meant to fix, now hidden behind a type assertion.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger(), discarding both the receiver's state and all contextual attributes, so tests exercising FromContext can capture neither the logs emitted downstream nor the context enrichment. Anyone writing tests for the new LoggerMiddleware.FromContext path gets a fake that silently swallows assertions — Message/Calls stay zero on the new logger — producing tests that pass while verifying nothing.

[ADVISORY] The PR is titled as a chore renaming instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware, but this file introduces an entirely new middleware (NewContextualLoggerMiddleware) with new behavior not traceable to the stated intent. Reviewers and future archaeologists auditing this commit for a rename will miss that plugin request logging architecture (contextual logger injection, log-field sourcing) changed underneath them; release notes/changelog for a 'chore' will not describe a logging behavior change.

[BUG] The refactor silently drops the traceID, pluginId, and endpoint fields from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line, replacing them only with attributes provided via the contextual logger — with no guarantee the fallback path carries them. Operators grepping 'grafana-data-egress' logs lose trace correlation (traceID) and endpoint identification for every plugin request whenever the contextual-attribute path is not populated; the grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext fallback at logger.go:51 returns d.New(), which carries none of these fields, so log consumers and any dashboards alerting on these fields break.

[ADVISORY] A new required method FromContext is added to the exported Logger interface as part of a rename chore, a breaking public-surface change forcing all external implementers to comply. Any out-of-tree implementation of plugins/log.Logger (plugin embedders, test doubles in downstream repos) fails to compile against this 'chore' release; the change is not flagged as breaking anywhere in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only instruments QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, and CollectMetrics, leaving SubscribeStream, PublishStream, and RunStream pass-throughs, so contextual logging coverage is incomplete. Stream endpoint logs produced deeper in the stack get no pluginId/endpoint/dsName context, an inconsistent observability surface introduced by the same diff that claims to centralize contextual logging; RunStream is long-lived, so this is the path where contextual logging matters most.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() that discards both the receiver's recorded state and the context's attributes, so any test asserting on the middleware's new FromContext-based logging inspects a logger that was never written to. Tests using the fake to verify the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line will read zero calls from the returned logger, producing false-passing or silently vacuous coverage for the very behavior this diff adds.

[ADVISORY] The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware is inserted between MetricsMiddleware and LoggerMiddleware, an ordering-sensitive placement where the contextual attributes must flow inward but the comment that previously documented the 'top of the stack' invariant (deleted from metrics_middleware.go lines 25-27) is not re-established at the new site. The next middleware reordering will silently break contextual plugin-request logging because the invariant that ContextualLoggerMiddleware must precede LoggerMiddleware (and follow TracingMiddleware for trace correlation) is now enforced only by position, with no test or comment in the diff guarding it.

[ADVISORY] The stream endpoints (SubscribeStream, PublishStream, RunStream) pass ctx through without calling instrumentContext, so the contextual-logger attributes are never attached on streaming paths. Any log emitted via logger.FromContext inside stream handling (RunStream handlers, downstream middlewares below this one on streaming requests) lacks pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname, and operators correlating stream-related plugin logs by datasource or user get nothing — the very fields this refactor exists to propagate.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently falls back to d.New() when the wrapped infra logger's FromContext does not return a *log.ConcreteLogger, discarding the context entirely rather than preserving contextual attributes. If pkg/infra/log ever returns a wrapped or alternate Logger type from FromContext (or the wrapped logger was constructed via a path that isn't ConcreteLogger), every 'Plugin Request Completed' line emitted by LoggerMiddleware.logRequest silently loses endpoint/pluginId/dsName/uname with no error signal — the log schema degrades invisibly, and the type assertion is a hidden coupling to infra/log's concrete type that breaks the abstraction the wrapper exists to provide.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver, so log output routed through FromContext is never recorded on the shared TestLogger instance tests assert against. Tests using TestLogger to verify middleware logging (e.g. that LoggerMiddleware emits 'Plugin Request Completed') now exercise the FromContext path introduced in this diff, and assertions on f.Calls/f.Message/f.InfoLogs stay green even if the production code logs nothing or logs the wrong thing — a stand-in that can go green while the real logging behavior regressed.

[ADVISORY] The logRequest path dropped the explicit traceID field (previously appended via tracing.TraceIDFromContext) and now relies entirely on the FromContext contextual logger to surface it. The 'Plugin Request Completed' / grafana-data-egress log lines, which downstream log-based alerting and dashboards key on traceID, now contain it only if the ConcreteLogger returned by infra log's FromContext injects traceID from ctx; if the fallback branch in grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext triggers (non-ConcreteLogger), traceID disappears from these lines with no compile-time or test signal — verify that a trace started by the outer TracingMiddleware actually reaches the ConcreteLogger before this relies on it.

[BUG] The rewrite of logRequest drops the traceID field from the "Plugin Request Completed" (grafana-data-egress) log line, and nothing in the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware re-adds it. The egress log previously correlated each plugin request to its trace via tracing.TraceIDFromContext; after this change operators querying the data-egress log by traceID get no matches, silently breaking log-trace correlation that existed before the rename. The contextual attributes added by instrumentContext (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) replace the removed fields, but traceID has no replacement source anywhere in this diff.

[ADVISORY] This PR is titled "Renamed instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware" (a chore/rename), but the diff actually splits contextual logging into a new middleware, changes the logging interface, and alters the egress log's field composition — objective drift well beyond a rename with no explicit acceptance in the change description. Anyone reviewing this as a mechanical rename (including automated release-note tooling and downstream backporters) misses that log field provenance changed from static middleware params to context-propagated contextual attributes; if infra log.FromContext filtering changes, egress logs lose pluginId/dsUID/uname with no local test guarding the composition of that log line.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of returning f, so any log emitted via the FromContext path is written to a discarded logger that no test can assert on. Tests exercising LoggerMiddleware through the new m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) call path get their assertions silently vacated — the "Plugin Request Completed" assertion (if any) still passes against the old recorded Calls, but new contextual-logger output is invisible; a future regression in FromContext wiring (e.g. always falling back to d.New()) passes unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] NewMetricsMiddleware retains the pre-existing pattern of capturing a single imw instance in the closure and mutating imw.next per wrap, while the contextual/metrics split removed the old "should live at the top of the middleware stack" contract comment that documented ordering invariants. The middleware stack in pluginsintegration.go is now ordered Tracing → Metrics → ContextualLogger → Logger; the removed comment was the only documentation of why the context-enriching middleware must sit above LoggerMiddleware, and NewContextualLoggerMiddleware placed below Metrics by convention alone means a future reorder silently drops all contextual fields from egress logs with no test or comment guarding it.

[ADVISORY] The exported Logger interface gains a required FromContext method, breaking every out-of-tree/existing implementer of plugins/log.Logger in one commit bundled into a rename PR. Any Grafana-internal or enterprise fork implementing plog.Logger directly fails to compile after this "chore" PR; the only conforming implementation and the fake are updated in-tree, so the break is invisible to CI here.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver, so all log calls made through the contextual logger are recorded on a throwaway instance invisible to the test. Any test asserting that LoggerMiddleware (which now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)) actually emitted 'Plugin Request Completed' via TestLogger's Logs/Calls fields will see zero calls and empty messages — assertions on f.InfoLogs will pass trivially only if they check nothing, or fail misleadingly; the fake silently discards the behavior it was extended to support.

[ADVISORY] The only test change in the diff is a constructor rename (newMetricsMiddleware); the contextual-logger behavior that moved from InstrumentationMiddleware.instrumentContext into the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware is verified by no test in this diff. Test files checked: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware_test.go (renamed, constructor-only change). Nothing in the diff asserts that instrumentContext's output (endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname contextual attributes) reaches the logger — if instrumentContext drops an attribute or ContextualLoggerMiddleware is mis-ordered in the middleware stack so FromContext sees a bare context, every existing test still passes and the data-egress logs silently lose plugin/datasource/user context in production.

[ADVISORY] logRequest no longer emits traceID (tracing.TraceIDFromContext removed) and instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go does not add it, so 'grafana-data-egress' logs lose trace correlation — and no test change in this diff would catch the regression. Operators correlating plugin request logs with distributed traces via traceID get logs with no trace identifier after this diff; the renamed/unchanged middleware tests assert nothing about traceID, so the attribute silently disappears.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently falls back to d.New() (dropping the contextual attributes) when the underlying logger is not *log.ConcreteLogger, and this branch has no test coverage in the diff. Any logger implementation whose FromContext returns a non-ConcreteLogger wrapper (nested wrappers, test doubles) makes the middleware chain's carefully attached endpoint/pluginId/dsName attributes vanish from 'Plugin Request Completed' logs with no error and no failing test; the fallback branch is never exercised by the diff's tests.

[BUG] The refactor drops traceID from the 'grafana-data-egress' audit log with no replacement source. The old logRequest appended tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx) to every Plugin Request Completed event; the new version only relies on contextual attributes set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware, which adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/uid/uname but no traceID (see contextual_logger_middleware.go instrumentContext). The 'grafana-data-egress' event consumers (audit/compliance pipelines that correlate egress log lines with request traces) lose traceID on every plugin request, and nothing in the diff surfaces that regression — the log line still emits 'status OK', so it reads as success.

[ADVISORY] LoggerMiddleware now depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being installed above it in the stack, with no structural guarantee and a silent-degradation failure mode. Any stack that constructs NewLoggerMiddleware without also adding NewContextualLoggerMiddleware (the type is exported and Grafana Enterprise historically wires these middlewares independently) logs 'Plugin Request Completed' events for grafana-data-egress with no pluginId, endpoint, uname, or dsName/dsUID — the event becomes unattributable, silently. The author's counter is 'the one call site in this diff was updated'; that survives only for OSS main and fails for every out-of-tree composition of these exported middlewares.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently discards all contextual attributes when the infra logger is not a *log.ConcreteLogger. If d.l.FromContext(ctx) returns any non-ConcreteLogger implementation (infra log wrappers/mock loggers used in tests or alternate builds), the type assertion fails and the method returns d.New(), a logger with zero request context — every plugin-request log line then omits pluginId/endpoint/uname with no error, warning, or observable signal. The operation still logs 'successfully', so operators never learn their egress logs are unattributed. Rebuttal: 'ConcreteLogger is the only real implementation' — but the wrapper pattern here exists precisely because that is not guaranteed, and the fallback is silent rather than logged.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of f, so all logs emitted via FromContext are invisible to the test's assertions. Any test that stubs a TestLogger into LoggerMiddleware and asserts on ErrorLogs/Calls for the new FromContext-based logging path sees zero calls — assertions pass vacuously and a future regression in the FromContext wiring would not fail any test. The strongest counter is 'callers can capture the returned logger'; that fails for middleware that calls FromContext internally and discards the original logger.

goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` doing `concreteInfraLogger, ok := d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)` and, on failure, returning `d.New()` (no ctx), which would drop any contextual attributes added via `log.WithContextualAttributes` (used by the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`) for the subsequent `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` call in `LoggerMiddleware`. However, from the diff alone we cannot verify that `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` can ever return a non-`*log.ConcreteLogger` (it likely is one), so the “feature becomes a no-op” claim is conditional and not provably a present defect just from this PR.

In CreateMiddlewares, this is satisfied only by the current slice order (pluginsintegration.go: `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` is placed before `NewLoggerMiddleware(...)`), with no comment/assertion/test enforcing it. adjudication.rationale: In `logger_middleware.go`, the explicit `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` extraction and `traceID` field append were removed, and the new `logParams` no longer includes `traceID`. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext` only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, datasource info, and `uname` via `log.WithContextualAttributes`, not `traceID`. The log line is now emitted as `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, but nothing in this diff guarantees that `FromContext` will re-derive and attach `traceID` (it delegates to infra logger behavior not shown here). Thus, the diff introduces a real risk/likely regression where `grafana-data-egress` logs lose `traceID` correlation data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new behavior-bearing middleware `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go` (with `instrumentContext` conditionally appending `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` and calling `log.WithContextualAttributes`). In `CreateMiddlewares` it is now wired into the middleware stack via `clientmiddleware.NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()`. The diff does not add any corresponding test file, and the only modified test is the renamed `metrics_middleware_test.go`, which no longer contains (and in this diff does not introduce) coverage for `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` or `instrumentContext`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test concern for newly introduced logic, not a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show LoggerMiddleware.logRequest no longer appends plugin/request identity fields itself (pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID) and instead logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go), relying on context enrichment done elsewhere (`instrumentContext` in the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware and `log.WithContextualAttributes`). It’s therefore true that if LoggerMiddleware is used without ContextualLoggerMiddleware, those fields won’t appear. However, the claim that there are other composition sites (tests/alternative wiring) that stack LoggerMiddleware without the new middleware is not verifiable from this diff alone—only `CreateMiddlewares` is shown and it was updated to include the pairing. So the coupling/implicit ordering is a real diff-grounded design concern, but the broader regression impact beyond the shown wiring can’t be confirmed here.

adjudication.rationale: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only calls instrumentContext() in QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics, while SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream just delegate to m.next without adding contextual attributes (contextual_logger_middleware.go). Since LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx), streaming paths will lack the plugin/request attributes that instrumentContext would have added. This is a real, diff-grounded completeness gap in the refactor’s contextual logging coverage, but it’s not a correctness/security defect.

That fallback would indeed drop any contextual attributes attached to `ctx` (e.g., via the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware using `log.WithContextualAttributes`), and it happens silently. However, the diff does not prove that `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` can return a non-*log.ConcreteLogger in current builds; the concern is about robustness/future wrappers/tests rather than a demonstrably failing path from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go the newly added method `func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger { return NewTestLogger() }` ignores the receiver and returns a fresh logger instance. This means any logs emitted via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (as added in LoggerMiddleware) will go to a different `TestLogger` than the one a test likely holds references to, so `Calls/Message/Ctx` on the original won’t be updated.
